newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine defense chiefs indicted over Ecuador arms.
newsitem.headline: Argentine defense chiefs indicted over Ecuador arms.

text.p: A former Argentine defence minister and Air Force chief were indicted on Monday by a federal judge investigating the illegal sale of arms to Ecuador during its border war with Peru last year, court officials said.

Federal Judge Jorge Urso's indictment of former minister Oscar Camilion and of retired Brigadier Gen. Juan Paulik makes them the top officials to be tried in the case. So far the head-of-state arms firm Fabricaciones Militares, Luis Sarlenga and some of his aides were the only ones charged.
Argentina has been severely embarrassed by the discovery of the sale of 5,000 Argentine FAL rifles and 75,000 tons of ammunition to Ecuador during the jungle border clash with Peru early last year.
Not only is Peru one of Argentina's closest Latin American allies, but Argentina was supposed to be one of the guarantors of the Rio Treaty peace deal between the two countries.
Camilion and Paulik are charged with "failing in their duties as public officials" -- by failing to stop the weapons shipments despite allegedly knowing of their destination.
President Carlos Menem's government insists the shipment in February last year was meant for Venezuela, but was diverted to the war zone without its knowledge.

However Judge Urso told reporters that both officials knew of the risk that weapons could be diverted to Ecuador, "but neither of them ever even picked up a telephone to find out if there was any news."

Camilion resigned in July after Judge Urso demanded his impeachment. Court officials quoted by the state-run news agency Telam said Urso also slapped a $100,000 embargo on property belonging to Camilion and Paulik.
